decision_card.headline: Meridian 4100 kit returned complete except one $14 neoprene shoulder strap; serial matches, no damage, no policy covers it.

evidence.label: Missing component
evidence.value: CMP-STRAP-NEO (Neoprene shoulder strap) - not serialized, not safety-critical, not essential. Only item missing.

evidence.label: Replacement cost
evidence.value: $14.00, in stock - 0.6% of the $2,400 declared kit value.

evidence.label: Serial check
evidence.value: Expected and received both 4100-SN-02201 - match confirmed, serial photo on file.

evidence.label: Everything else returned
evidence.value: Body, battery, charger, body cap, USB-C cable, foam case, rail clip all present. No unexpected components.

evidence.label: Inspection evidence
evidence.value: Complete - exterior photo, serial photo, completed checklist, inspector INSP-114, weight check pass. No missing fields.

evidence.label: Inspector notes
evidence.value: Empty - no free text submitted, so nothing to flag.

evidence.label: Approved policy
evidence.value: Zero active policies for this exception family; no matches and no near-misses.

evidence.label: Tool failures
evidence.value: None - all four lookups returned cleanly.

decision_card.recommended_action: Charge the customer $14.00 for CMP-STRAP-NEO, release the kit to resale stock, and close the case. No hold on the kit - the strap is a stock accessory and the body is verified by serial.
uncertainty: No outbound proof the strap physically shipped - the shortfall is derived from the kit BOM, not a dock photo of that specific item. If a pick error is plausible, the charge is wrong.
Whether $14 is worth billing at all versus waiving as goodwill; that is a commercial call I have no guidance on.
No customer history reviewed - I cannot tell whether CUST-SYN-801 is a first-time or repeat short-return, which might change the response.
Customer notes were not present in the case record, so I cannot confirm the customer agrees the strap is missing.

proposed_boundaries.description: Exactly one missing component, and it is non-serialized, non-safety-critical, and non-essential.
proposed_boundaries.reason: Multiple missing items, or anything serialized or essential, suggests a different failure than a dropped accessory and deserves fresh eyes.

proposed_boundaries.description: Replacement cost at or below $25 and at or below 2% of declared kit value.
proposed_boundaries.reason: Caps worst-case auto-charge exposure and keeps the rule from silently scaling up on high-value kits where 2% is still real money.

proposed_boundaries.description: Expected and received serials match, and the component is in_stock.
proposed_boundaries.reason: A serial mismatch means the wrong or a swapped unit came back - a bigger problem than an accessory. In-stock keeps the charge equal to true replaceable cost.

proposed_boundaries.description: Inspection evidence complete with zero missing fields, no new damage, and no unexpected components.
proposed_boundaries.reason: The charge rests entirely on the completed checklist and weight check. Incomplete evidence means the shortfall is not actually established.

proposed_boundaries.description: Zero tool failures across all lookups in the case.
proposed_boundaries.reason: A silent lookup failure could hide a second missing item or a wrong price; a partial picture must never auto-charge.

proposed_boundaries.description: Inspector and customer notes are empty, or contain no dispute over what shipped and no embedded instruction; any instruction-like text routes to a human.
proposed_boundaries.reason: A disputed shortfall is a judgment call, and note text must never be able to steer an automated charge.

proposed_boundaries.description: Charge only; never auto-waive, never place a hold, never touch the customer's deposit beyond the itemized amount.
proposed_boundaries.reason: Keeps the automated action to a single reversible line item with a clear audit trail.

decision_card.why_human_must_decide: No active policy exists for missing-accessory returns, so there is no rule to apply. This is the first case of its kind, meaning your decision sets the dollar threshold and the charge-vs-waive default for every similar return that follows. Deterministic code performs the charge only after you approve.
